lawyer:
Mr. A.Q.M. Fazlul Haque ------- For the petitioners. 
Mr. M. Hashmatullah Sheikh ------- For the opposite parties.
parties:
Md. Rakibul Islam and Others
Vs.
Anwar Hossain and Another
full_judgment:
Faruque Ahmed, J: This rule at the instance of the plaintiff petitioners was issued calling upon the opposite parties No. 1-2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.09.1998 and 29.09.1998 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Shariatpur in Title Appeal No. 23 of 1996 reversing those dated 27.04.1996 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Bhedargonj, Shariatpur in Title Suit No. 11 of 1993 should not be set aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. On 03.03.93 plaintiff (petitioner herein) filed Title Suit No. 11 of 1993 in the court of Assistant Judge, Bhederganj, District Shariatpur against defendants Anwar Hossain Gazi, Shahanara Begum and Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh as defendant Nos.1,2 and 3 for specific performance of contract for selling 1.95 acres of land for a consideration of Tk. 15,000/-, stating inter alia, that the suit land of Felir Char Mouza and Moheshkhali Mouza within police station Bhederganj district Shariatpur belonged to Fatejan Bibi, the mother of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and after her death the defendants inherited the suit land and that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 verbally agreed in January, 1987 to sell it to the plaintiff. Iman Hossain, their elder brother also verbally agreed to sell his portion of land measuring .66 decimals of the said Mouza to the plaintiff. Talks were held in presence of witnesses and that the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 received Tk. 10,000/- out of Tk. 15,000/- as consideration money from the plaintiff as well as through P.Ws 3 and 4 and that the defendant No.1 wrote three letters to the plaintiff as well as to his father asking for money and accordingly Tk. 2000/- was paid on 19.01.87 to the defendants through P.W. 3 Chhitu Khan by the plaintiff as advance and that thereafter in the month of June, 1988 the plaintiff along with Md. Ali Madbar went to the house of defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and paid them Tk. 4,000/- and requested them to execute and register kabala they assured him that they would do the same after finishing the criminal case in the name of the husband of defendant No. 2 and that in the meantime, Iman Hossain elder brother of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2, executed and registered kabala of his .66 decimals of land as agreed upon Verbally in favour of the plaintiff in the middle of August, 1989 after receiving Tk. 5,000/- as value of the land and that thereafter being informed the younger brother of the plaintiff along with Md. Ali Madbar went to the house of the defendants in Lashmipur and paid Taka 4,000/- on 10.03.90 and it was decided that the defendants would come to the house of plaintiff at Bhederganj and execute and register the kabala in favour of the plaintiff just after the judgment of the case of the husband of defendant No. 2 is pronounced. It may he mentioned here that at the time of handing over possession of the land of Iman Hossain Gazi to the plaintiff after registration of the kabala, in 1989 the possession of the suit land was handed over to the plaintiff by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. That in the middle of 1991 defendant Nos. 1 and 2 assured the plaintiff not to worry about the registration of kabala since the plaintiff is their relation and is already in possession. That kabala not being registered inspite of such assurance, in the last week of November, 1992 plaintiff sent his younger brother Awlad Hossain to the defendants for receiving the balance money and registering kabala which was refused by them, then the plaintiff sent his father to the defendants for the purpose who was also refused and that the plaintiff paid in total Tk. 10,000/- out of Taka 15,000/- of consideration money and he is in possession of the suit land and as such the defendants are liable to execute and register kabala in favour of the plaintiff. Hence, the plaintiff instituted the suit against the defendants for a decree. 

 5. P.Ws and 2 D.Ws were examined in support of their respective cases. The learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record by his judgment and decree dated 27.04.1996 decreed the suit. As against that the defendant petitioners preferred Title Appeal No. 23 of 1996 in the Court of the District Judge, Shariatpur and the learned Subordinate judge, 2nd Court, Shariatpur who heard the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 24.09.1998 allowed the appeal. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid appellate judgment and decree, the plaintiff petitioner obtained the present rule. 

 7. Mr. A.Q.M. Fazlul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner placed the revisional application, the plaint and written statements, the depositions of the P.Ws and D.Ws and submitted that the learned trial Court having found that the plaintiff was able to prove his case and accordingly decreed the suit, but the learned appellate Court on misreading and non consideration the material on evidence on record committed error in allowing the appeal dismissing the suit. The learned Advocate further submitted that though the plaintiff examined 6 P.Ws including the plaintiff in support of his agreement for sale of the suit land, payment of consideration and taking of delivery of possession in the suit land, the learned trial Court as well as the appellate Court did not give any finding as to the taking/delivery of possession to the plaintiff by the defendants and that the appellate Court committed error in law in allowing the appeal without giving any finding as to whether the plaintiff was able to prove his possession in the suit land and as such the learned Advocate for the petitioner prayed that the case may be sent to the learned appellate Court on remand for passing a proper judgment afresh by the learned appellate Court. The learned Advocate further submitted that the finding by the learned appellate Court that all the P.Ws being close relative of the plaintiff committed error in disbelieving them although there was no contradiction in their deposition regarding the disputed the agreement with the defendants and taking of delivery of possession of the suit land by the plaintiff. The learned Advocate for the petitioner also submitted that the P.Ws are also related to the defendants. 

 9. On perusal of the judgment passed by the learned trial Court, it appears, the learned trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record found that exhibit-1, 1(ka) and 1(kha) written by the defendant No.1 Anwar Hossain asking the plaintiff to make payment of the consideration money and that had there been no such agreement for sale by the defendants why the defendant would ask for money by those exhibits, and that those exhibits are genuine and those were written by defendant No.1 Anwar Hossain; that defendant No. 1 though denied his signature in the written statement and vokalatnama, but he is contesting the case. The learned trial Court further held that P.W.1 Anwar Hossain deposed falsely before the Court and stated that he does not know the plaintiff, he admitted that his brother Imam Hossain sold his share of the same land to the son of the plaintiff which shows that he deposed falsely that he does not know the plaintiff. The learned trial Court further found that the defendant No.1 and 2 took taka 10,000/- from the plaintiff for sale of the suit land and that the suit is not barred by time. With these findings the learned trial Court decreed the suit. 

 10. On appeal, the learned appellate Court it appears, held that the plaintiff did not state that the defendants were present at the talk of sale held at the residence of the plaintiff; that Billal Hossain Bala, Mohammad Ali and Habibullah who allegedly were present in the talk for sale, they had not been produced before the Court but some other persons like Ali Matbor, Chhita Kha, Hedayetullah were produced before the Court as witnesses; that some of the P.Ws stated that there was a bainapatra for sale of the suit land, but in fact there was no such bainapatra between the plaintiff and the defendant; that the three letters exhibit-1 series were not written by the same person, signatures of the writer are not same; that the signature given in the deposition is not quite similar to the signature put in the three letters exhibit-1 series; that hand writing expert could not give any opinion as to whether the writings, signature of exhibit-1 series are similar to the signatures put in written statement. vokalatnama and deposition by the defendants; all the P.Ws admitted that no consideration was given to the defendants at the time of Baina though there is a custom in the locality to give a token money for bainapatra; that nothing stated in the plaint as to who handed over possession of the suit land to the plaintiff; that P.W.4 Awalad Hossain stated in cross-examination that the defendants were present at the talk of sale but in the plaint of the suit no such statement has been made; that the family of the plaintiff has got more then 60 bighas of land, so he cannot acquire the suit land beyond the maximum ceiling; that there is contradiction in the deposition of P.Ws. 5 and 6 regarding the date of talk of sale; that P.Ws 2-6 cannot say the number of suit plots and khatians; that P.W.2 stated that Imam Hossain brother of the defendant No.1 handed over possession of the suit land to the plaintiff; that P.W. 2,4,5 and 6 are plaintiff's father, brother and other relatives and P.W.3 is his day labourer; that P.W.1 cannot say the quantum of land plot wise; that the plaintiff is the distant relative of the defendants; that D.W.1 denied his signature in the written statement, vokalatnama of the present suit; D.W.1 admitted that his brother Imam Hossain executed and registered a kabala in favour of the plaintiff in the year 1989 transferring his share to the plaintiff; that though the defendants (D.W.2) denies his signature in the written statement and vokalatnama, but in fact he gave his signature in the written statement and vokalatanma of the case; that the value of the suit land taka 15,000/- was a proper one; that plaintiff was directed to produce Imam Hossain, Billal Hossain, Mohammad Ali and Habibullah, but Imam Hossain only was dead, and the plaintiff failed to produce others as witnesses. With these findings the learned appellate Court allowed the appeal setting aside the decree passed by the learned trial Court. 

 11. On perusal of the plaint of the suit, it appears, in the plaint it has been stated that the plaintiff got possession in the suit land through Imam Hossain, but the learned appellate Court found that no such statement is there in the plaint. So, the learned appellate Court was not justified in holding that no such statement has been made in the plaint. The learned appellate Court further held that the plaintiff having owned more then 60 bighas of land he is not entitled to get a decree for the suit land under law. It appears this is not the case of either of the parties and as such this finding is, in my opinion, unwarranted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
